## 1. GLOBAL MACRO OVERVIEW

The macro backdrop entering this week is defined by a sharp tension between resilient equity markets and a bond market signaling higher-for-longer rates. The S&P 500 has posted 18 record highs this year and is set to record its fastest quarterly earnings growth since 2021, with non-Magnificent Seven companies growing earnings 17.4% in Q1 — the strongest such performance since Q4 2021 [Source: https://www.marketwatch.com/story/these-underdogs-are-a-big-reason-s-p-500-profit-growth-is-the-fastest-in-nearly-5-years-4a43f142]. Yet bond investors are demanding compensation for inflation risk, pushing the 10-year Treasury yield to 4.57% — its highest level in a year — while the 2-year sits at 4.08%, yielding a still-inverted curve that has narrowed to its tightest 5s30s spread (83 basis points) since May 2025 [Source: https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2026-05-25/treasury-curve-flashes-higher-for-longer-warning-under-warsh].

U.S. CPI came in at 3.95% year-on-year (as of April), while PPI surged 2.66% month-on-month, reflecting the energy shock driven by the Iran conflict and Strait of Hormuz closure [Source: https://fred.stlouisfed.org/series/CPIAUCSL]. The personal consumption expenditures (PCE) price index is expected to print 3.8% year-on-year for April when released Thursday — a figure that would cement the "higher-for-longer" narrative under new Fed Chair Kevin Warsh, who was sworn in Friday at what analysts describe as a pivotal moment for monetary policy [Source: https://finance.yahoo.com/economy/policy/articles/more-war-driven-inflation-seen-115519421.html]. The effective Fed Funds Rate currently stands at 3.64%, leaving a significant gap between the policy rate and inflation [Source: https://fred.stlouisfed.org/series/FEDFUNDS].

The Iran war, now nearly three months old, remains the dominant geopolitical and macro risk. Fresh U.S. military strikes in southern Iran on Monday/Tuesday have dampened prospects for an imminent peace deal, reversing earlier optimism after Trump's Saturday statement that a memorandum of understanding had been "largely negotiated." Oil prices have swung violently — Brent fell nearly $5 on Monday as deal hopes emerged, then rebounded 2-3% Tuesday on news of fresh strikes [Source: https://www.cnbc.com/2026/05/26/oil-prices-today-brent-wti-iran-trump-hormuz.html]. Analysts warn oil could stay above $100 for years if the Strait remains closed, which would keep inflation structurally elevated [Source: https://oilprice.com/Energy/Crude-Oil/Oil-Could-Stay-Above-100-for-Years-Analysts-Warn.html].

The global growth picture is becoming more differentiated. KOSPI surged 2.55% today on Korean risk-on momentum, while Japan's Nikkei slipped -0.25% and Australia's ASX 200 fell -0.39%, reflecting Asian divergence as higher rates and energy costs weigh on import-heavy economies. In an emergency response to the Iran war's inflationary spillover, Sri Lanka's central bank stunned markets with a 100-basis-point rate hike to 8.75% — the largest increase since March 2023 — citing a depreciating rupee and surging energy costs [Source: https://www.reuters.com/world/asia-pacific/sri-lanka-raises-key-policy-rate-by-100-bps-offset-gulf-crisis-pain-2026-05-26/]. This week's compressed calendar — Memorial Day shortened the U.S. session Monday — front-loads critical data into Thursday's 8:30am session, with Q1 GDP, Core PCE, durable goods, jobless claims, and new home sales all dropping simultaneously [Source: https://www.barchart.com/story/news/2109089/gdp-earnings-and-other-key-things-to-watch-this-week].

- [Report describes the 10-year Treasury yield at "its highest level in a year"]: The bundle's CNN source does state "US Treasury yields...are trading at their highest levels in a year," which supports the claim. However, the FRED data only provides the yield as of May 21 (4.57%), so the claim cannot be independently verified as of the report date of May 26.
- [Report claims gold "dropped by just over 10%" since the Iran war began in February]: This figure comes solely from the Forbes/Mark Cuban article, which is a commentary piece, not a primary data source. The bundle's price data only shows gold at $4,526.50 on May 26 with no historical baseline for February; the claim cannot be confirmed against bundle data.
